tools.name: vice_ping
tools.description: Check if VICE is responding

tools.name: vice_memory_read
tools.description: Read a memory range, optionally from a named bank. The machine halts; the answer's runState reports it. sideEffects defaults to false: reading a register such as $D019 with side effects (which clears pending IRQ flags) needs sideEffects true.

address.description: Address: number, hex string ($1000), or symbol name

bank.description: Optional: Memory bank name (e.g., 'ram' to read RAM under ROM). Use vice_memory_banks to list available banks.

encoding.description: Optional: 'hex' (default) returns one compact hex string; 'array' returns the bytes as an array of numbers.

sideEffects.description: Stock-only, optional, default false: whether the read is permitted to have side effects (e.g. reading $D019 clears pending VIC-II IRQ flags). Defaults to side-effect-free.

tools.name: vice_memory_write
tools.description: Write to memory

address.description: Address: number, hex string ($1000), or symbol name

bank.description: Optional: memory bank name (for example 'ram' to write the RAM under ROM). Defaults to the CPU view, which follows $00/$01 banking. Use vice_memory_banks to list available banks.

tools.name: vice_memory_banks
tools.description: List available memory banks

tools.name: vice_registers_get
tools.description: Get CPU registers

tools.name: vice_registers_set
tools.description: Set one CPU register. Values are integers within the register's width (8 or 16 bits). The answer reports the value the emulator read back.

register.description: Register name as vice_registers_available lists it (stock VICE 3.8: PC, A, X, Y, SP, 00, 01, FL, LIN, CYC). The processor flags are one register, FL; the single flag names N, V, B, D, I, Z and C are refused.

tools.name: vice_registers_available
tools.description: Lists every register the connected VICE build enumerates via REGISTERS_AVAILABLE, with each register's wire id, name, and width -- the width the emulator itself reports, in BITS (8 or 16 on a 6510), taken verbatim from REGISTERS_AVAILABLE's size byte.

tools.name: vice_execution_pause
tools.description: Pause execution

tools.name: vice_execution_run
tools.description: Resume execution

tools.name: vice_execution_step
tools.description: Step one or more instructions. Refused while runState is "unknown": call vice_execution_pause or vice_execution_run first to establish a known state.

tools.name: vice_execution_until_return
tools.description: Run until the current subroutine returns. This differs from vice_execution_step with stepOver, which steps over one call instead of running out of the current one. Refused while runState is "unknown", like vice_execution_step.

tools.name: vice_checkpoint_add
tools.description: Add a checkpoint (breakpoint). stop:false needs acknowledgeTraceRisk:true, because a non-stopping checkpoint reports every hit from inside the emulator's CPU loop and can stall the emulator on a hot address. Set a condition afterwards with vice_checkpoint_set_condition.

start.description: Start address: number, hex string ($1000), or symbol name

end.description: End address: number, hex, or symbol (optional, default=start)

exec.description: Break on execution. Default true only when none of load, store and exec is given; if you give any of them, only the ones set true apply, and setting all false is refused.

acknowledgeTraceRisk.description: Stock-only, optional, default false: required (set true) when stop:false -- a non-stopping checkpoint emits one CHECKPOINT_INFO frame per hit synchronously from inside the emulator's CPU loop, over the blocking monitor socket, and can stall the emulator on a hot address. The client rate-limits hits per second and auto-disables the checkpoint if the limit is exceeded.

tools.name: vice_checkpoint_delete
tools.description: Delete checkpoint

tools.name: vice_checkpoint_list
tools.description: List all checkpoints

tools.name: vice_checkpoint_toggle
tools.description: Enable/disable checkpoint

tools.name: vice_checkpoint_set_condition
tools.description: Set a checkpoint condition, as a string (for example 'A == $42'; RL and CY name the raster line and the cycle in the line) or as an object with a 'kind' field ('comparison', 'and' or 'or'). A condition cannot be cleared or replaced once set, so setting one on a checkpoint that has one is refused.

condition.description: Either a condition expression string (for example 'A == $42') or an object with a 'kind' field ('comparison', 'and' or 'or'). This property declares no "type", because the schema subset the checker supports has no way to say "string or object".

tools.name: vice_watch_add
tools.description: Add a memory watchpoint with an optional condition (a checkpoint on load and store). stop:false needs acknowledgeTraceRisk:true, as for vice_checkpoint_add.

address.description: Address: number, hex string ($1000), or symbol name

condition.description: Condition expression for conditional watchpoint. Supported: 'A == $xx', 'X == $xx', 'Y == $xx', 'PC == $xxxx', 'SP == $xx'. For store watches, condition is evaluated after the store completes.

stop.description: Stock-only, optional, default true: stop execution when hit. Set false (with acknowledgeTraceRisk:true) for a non-stopping trace watchpoint.

acknowledgeTraceRisk.description: Stock-only, optional, default false: required (set true) when stop:false, identically to vice_checkpoint_add's acknowledgeTraceRisk.

tools.name: vice_machine_reset
tools.description: Reset the machine (soft or hard). run_after defaults to false, so the machine stays halted after the reset; pass run_after:true to resume it.

mode.description: Reset mode: 'soft' (CPU reset, default) or 'hard' (power cycle)

run_after.description: Default false: the machine stays halted after the reset. Pass true to resume it.

tools.name: vice_autostart
tools.description: Autostart a PRG or disk image. On stock, program (load-by-name) is refused -- AUTOSTART supports only a numeric index field and has no load-by-name field; use index to select a program by position instead.

path.description: Path to PRG file or disk image (.d64, .g64, .prg)

program.description: Refused on stock: AUTOSTART has no load-by-name field. Use index instead.

tools.name: vice_disk_attach
tools.description: Attach a disk image to a drive. Only unit 8 is reachable on stock VICE: units 9-11 are refused instead of being attached to unit 8. The attach is an AUTOSTART with the run flag clear.

unit.description: Drive unit (8-11). Only unit 8 is reachable on stock; units 9-11 are refused.

tools.name: vice_snapshot_save
tools.description: Save complete emulator state to a named snapshot (DUMP). Use this to capture a debugging checkpoint that can be restored later with vice_snapshot_load. A JSON metadata sidecar is written alongside the snapshot as this client's own bookkeeping.

name.description: Unique name for this snapshot (alphanumeric, underscore, hyphen only). Choose descriptive names like 'before_crash' or 'level3_boss_fight'.

description.description: Human-readable description of what state this snapshot captures.

include_roms.description: Include ROM images in snapshot (default: false).

include_disks.description: Include disk drive state in snapshot (default: false).

tools.name: vice_snapshot_load
tools.description: Restore emulator state from a saved snapshot. A missing snapshot is refused, and the refusal names the snapshots found on disk.

name.description: Name of the snapshot to load. Must match the name previously given to vice_snapshot_save.

tools.name: vice_keyboard_type
tools.description: Type text into the C64 keyboard buffer. By default both upper- and lowercase ASCII letters type as the capitals of the power-on charset, so BASIC commands work in either case. The machine halts; the bytes stay queued until you resume it.

text.description: Text to type (converts to PETSCII). Use \n for Return.

petscii_upper.description: Default true: ASCII A-Z and a-z both map to PETSCII $41-$5A (capitals in the power-on charset). Set false to send each byte unchanged (a-z then shows as graphics in the power-on charset).

tools.name: vice_keyboard_petscii
tools.description: Feed exact PETSCII bytes into the KERNAL keyboard buffer

data.description: Exact PETSCII bytes to feed to the KERNAL keyboard buffer (1-255 each; 13 is Return)

tools.name: vice_joystick_set
tools.description: Hold or release joystick switches on C64 control port 1 or 2. A hold attaches VICE's "Joyport I/O simulation" device to that port (the only device the binary monitor can drive); a release (direction center, fire false) puts back the port's previous device. While a switch is held, bits 5-7 of the port's CIA register read 0. The answer reports the CIA register ($DC01 for port 1, $DC00 for port 2) as read back. The machine halts; resume it to let the program see the switches.

direction.description: Direction: up, down, left, right, center, or array for diagonals

tools.name: vice_disassemble
tools.description: Disassemble memory to 6502 instructions. The disassembly is computed in the client. Reading memory halts the machine, and runState reports it. An illegal opcode that ACME's !cpu 6510 cannot express shows as !byte with the mnemonic in a comment.

address.description: Start address: number, hex string ($1000), or symbol name

count.description: Number of instructions (default 10, max 100). Mutually exclusive with end.

end.description: Stock-only, optional: last address of the range. Mutually exclusive with count.

show_symbols.description: Show symbol names where the operand's role and width prove substitution cannot change the encoding (default true). With no symbol store loaded this is a no-op and the answer says so.

bank.description: Optional: memory bank name (e.g. ram to disassemble the RAM under ROM). Defaults to the CPU view, which follows $00/$01 banking. Use vice_memory_banks to list available banks.

tools.name: vice_memory_search
tools.description: Search memory for a byte pattern, with an optional wildcard mask. The search is computed in the client. The pattern is refused when it is longer than the range or longer than 4096 bytes. The mask must be exactly as long as the pattern. max_results defaults to 100 and is refused above 10000. A range of all 64K is allowed.

start.description: Start address: number, hex string ($C000), or symbol name

end.description: End address: number, hex string ($FFFF), or symbol name

pattern.description: Byte pattern to find, e.g., [0x4C, 0x00, 0xA0] for JMP $A000. Refused if longer than the range searched or longer than 4096 bytes.

mask.description: Per-byte mask: 0xFF=exact match, 0x00=wildcard (optional). Must be exactly patterns length; never padded.

bank.description: Stock-only, optional: memory bank name (e.g. ram to search the RAM under ROM/I-O, io for the register view). Defaults to the CPU view (wire bank 0), which follows $00/$01 banking. The answer always reports which view it read. Use vice_memory_banks to list available banks.

tools.name: vice_memory_compare
tools.description: Compare two memory ranges byte by byte. The comparison is computed in the client. mode:ranges is served. mode:snapshot is refused, because no tool saves a memory-only snapshot.

mode.description: Comparison mode. ranges is served on stock; snapshot is refused with an explanatory message (no memory-only snapshot producer tool exists on either backend).

range1_start.description: Start address of first range (for mode=ranges): number, hex string ($1000), or symbol

range1_end.description: End address of first range (for mode=ranges): number, hex string ($1FFF), or symbol

range2_start.description: Start address of second range (for mode=ranges): number, hex string ($2000), or symbol. range2_end is derived from range1s length, never its own argument.

snapshot_name.description: Declared for argument compatibility; mode snapshot is not implemented on stock.

start.description: Declared for argument compatibility; mode snapshot is not implemented on stock.

end.description: Declared for argument compatibility; mode snapshot is not implemented on stock.

bank.description: Stock-only, optional: memory bank name applied to BOTH ranges (e.g. ram to compare the RAM under ROM/I-O). Defaults to the CPU view (wire bank 0), which follows $00/$01 banking. The answer always reports which view it read. Use vice_memory_banks to list available banks.

tools.name: vice_symbols_load
tools.description: Load a VICE-format label file (lines 'al C:xxxx .name') into the client's symbol table. Relative paths resolve from the project root. A label name that ACME could not parse is refused. Only format auto and vice are served; kickasm and simple are refused by name.

path.description: Path to symbol file (.sym, .lbl). Resolved against the workspace root and refused if it escapes, including via a symlink, with a 2 MiB / 50000-line / 20000-symbol ceiling.

format.description: Format: auto (default) or vice parse VICE-format al C:xxxx .Name lines on stock; kickasm and simple are refused by name -- no in-repo producer emits them.

tools.name: vice_symbols_lookup
tools.description: Look up a symbol by name, or the symbol at an address, in the client's symbol table. Exactly one of name or address is required; both together are refused.

name.description: Symbol name to look up (returns address). Exactly one of name or address is required.

address.description: Address to look up (returns symbol name): number, $hex string or symbol name. Exactly one of name or address is required.

tools.name: vice_vicii_get_state
tools.description: Get the VIC-II chip state, decoded in the client from one read of the $D000-$D02E registers. The pointers in $D018 are bank-relative: vice_cia_get_state (cia:2) or vice_sprite_get gives absolute addresses. Six internal fields (raster IRQ latch, video and row counters, bad-line condition, border flip-flops, sprite DMA state) cannot be read from the binary monitor and are listed under `unavailable` as {available:false, reason}, never as 0.

tools.name: vice_cia_get_state
tools.description: Get CIA1 and/or CIA2 state, decoded in the client from one read per chip of its 16 registers. The read has no side effects, so $DC0D and $DD0D are not cleared. Some addresses read back something other than what is written there. The readable side has its own name (for example timerA.current, interruptStatus). The write-only side (timerALatch, timerBLatch, interruptEnableMask, todAlarmTime, todLatchState) is listed under `unavailable` as {available:false, reason}, never as 0.

cia.description: CIA chip number: 1 or 2 (optional, default returns both)

tools.name: vice_sprite_get
tools.description: Get position, colour and control bits for one sprite or all eight. The client resolves the VIC bank ($DD00), the screen base ($D018) and the sprite pointer table with three reads. Sprite pointers are given as absolute dataAddress values. Omit `sprite` to get all eight.

sprite.description: Sprite number 0-7 (omit to get all sprites)

tools.name: vice_sprite_inspect
tools.description: Render one sprite's 63-byte data block as an ASCII or binary grid at native resolution (24 columns high-res, 12 columns multicolour, always 21 rows), with no scaling for the X/Y expansion bits. format:'png_base64' is not supported and is refused by name.

format.description: Output format: 'ascii' (default) or 'binary'. 'png_base64' is not supported and is refused by name.

tools.name: vice_cycles_stopwatch
tools.description: Measure elapsed CPU cycles for timing-critical code analysis. Use 'reset' to start timing, 'read' to get elapsed cycles, or 'reset_and_read' for atomic read-and-reset. Ideal for measuring raster routine timing. On VICE >= 3.10 the figure is exact (CPUHISTORY_GET); below 3.10 it is a within-one-frame reconstruction from LIN/CYC, and a bracket that crossed a frame boundary is refused rather than approximated. On the cpu_history route "cyclesExact" carries the uint64 delta as an exact decimal STRING and is always authoritative: "cycles" is that value narrowed to a JS number, so when the delta exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER the narrowing rounds and "exactness" reads "exact-but-narrowed" with a "caveat" saying so -- use cyclesExact for any arithmetic that matters.

action.description: Action to perform: 'reset' (start timing), 'read' (get elapsed cycles), or 'reset_and_read' (atomic read and reset)

tools.name: vice_run_until
tools.description: Resume the machine and wait until it stops, with a temporary checkpoint at address. The wait ends on any stop: this address (reached true), another checkpoint or watch, a CPU JAM, or any other entry to the monitor. stoppedBy says what stopped it (kind target, checkpoint, jam or other) and pc gives the stop address. If nothing stops the machine within timeout_ms, the answer has timedOut true. machineHalted is on every answer; when it is false the run state is unknown, and machineHaltedNote names the next call. cycles is not supported and is refused. Unknown argument names are refused.

address.description: Target address: number, hex, or symbol (stops when PC reaches this)

cycles.description: Not supported, and refused whenever present. Bound the wait with timeout_ms instead.

timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait for a stop before giving up; default 30000, clamped to 600000.

tools.name: vice_device_console
tools.description: Reaches VICE's text monitor over the -remotemonitor channel and halts the machine for the duration of the command, exactly as a binary-monitor command does. Issues the single allowlisted verb "device c:", resetting the current default device (memspace) back to the main CPU. Use this after a drive checkpoint hit leaves default_memspace pointed at a drive unit -- ADVANCE_INSTRUCTIONS and EXECUTE_UNTIL_RETURN then step the wrong CPU, and a bank-qualified checkpoint condition fails outright, until this is issued. This is an explicit tool, not auto-healing: nothing on the binary-side stepping path calls it automatically.

tools.name: vice_warp_set
tools.description: Reaches VICE's text monitor over the -remotemonitor channel and halts the machine for the duration of the command, exactly as a binary-monitor command does. Issues "warp on" or "warp off" depending on "enabled". There is no runtime WarpMode *resource* on stock -- measured err=0x01 OBJECT_MISSING over RESOURCE_GET -- so this is the only way to toggle warp at runtime on this backend; warp requested at launch time (-warp / InitialWarpMode) is a separate mechanism this tool does not touch. The response reports warp's own OBSERVED state rather than assuming the write took.

enabled.description: true issues "warp on", false issues "warp off".

tools.name: vice_memmap_show
tools.description: Reaches VICE's text monitor over the -remotemonitor channel and issues the single allowlisted verb "memmapshow", returning a structured, adjacency-merged access map in which execute is its own bit, for both RAM and ROM, never folded into a read. "startAddress", "endAddress" and "maxRanges" are client-side projection filters applied AFTER parsing -- none of the three ever reaches the socket, and the dialed command is always the frozen literal "memmapshow". An address with no recorded access is reported only via the gap between "addressesWithRecordedAccess" and "addressesQueried" -- never rendered, named, or implied as data.

startAddress.description: Inclusive lower bound of the projection filter: number, $hex string or symbol name. Defaults to 0. Applied after parsing, never sent to the text monitor.

endAddress.description: Inclusive upper bound of the projection filter: number, $hex string or symbol name. Defaults to 65535. Applied after parsing, never sent to the text monitor.

maxRanges.description: Hard ceiling on the number of emitted merged ranges. Defaults to 256, clamped to 4096 regardless of what is requested.

tools.name: vice_memmap_zap
tools.description: Reaches VICE's text monitor over the -remotemonitor channel and halts the machine for the duration of the command, exactly as a binary-monitor command does. Issues the single allowlisted verb "memmapzap", which clears the emulator's accumulated memory-access map, and then "memmapshow", so the returned "addressesWithRecordedAccess" and "addressesQueried" are observable proof the map was cleared, never a bare acknowledgement. Takes no parameters at all. An address with no recorded access is reported only via the gap between "addressesWithRecordedAccess" and "addressesQueried" -- never rendered, named, or implied as data.

tools.name: vice_cpu_history
tools.description: Reaches VICE's text monitor over the -remotemonitor channel and halts the machine for the duration of the command, exactly as a binary-monitor command does. Issues "chis" (or "chis N" for a caller-chosen decimal row count -- the ONE place that string is built, and validated/rendered there, never here), returning the decoded CPU-history entries -- address, raw bytes, disassembly, registers, processor flags and cycle count -- in the emulator's own emitted order. "chis" is compiled behind the same build-time flag as vice_memmap_show's "memmapshow"; a build without --enable-cpuhistory is reported as a named missing capability with its remedy, never a parse error.

count.description: Number of most-recent history rows to request. Omitted dials the bare "chis" verb.

tools.name: vice_profile_flat
tools.description: Reaches VICE's text monitor over the -remotemonitor channel and halts the machine for the duration of the command, exactly as a binary-monitor command does. Issues "prof flat" (or "prof flat N" for a caller-chosen decimal row count, validated/rendered by the transport's own builder), returning ranked cycle counts by address -- total and self cycles, each with a percentage -- in the emulator's own rank order (highest first). "prof flat" carries no build-time guard at all.

count.description: Number of ranked rows to request. Omitted dials the bare "prof flat" verb.

tools.name: vice_backtrace
tools.description: Reaches VICE's text monitor over the -remotemonitor channel and halts the machine for the duration of the command, exactly as a binary-monitor command does. Issues the bare, unparameterized "bt" verb -- "depth" never reaches the wire; it truncates the PARSED frame list client-side, since "bt" itself takes no wire parameter -- returning the current-PC frame plus the reconstructed JSR-chain frames in the emulator's own emitted order, each with its origin, callee, SP offset, raw bytes and disassembly.

depth.description: Max stack frames to show (default: 16, max: 64). A client-side projection filter applied to the PARSED frame list -- "bt" itself takes no wire parameter.

tools.name: vice_io_registers
tools.description: Reaches VICE's text monitor over the -remotemonitor channel and halts the machine for the duration of the command, exactly as a binary-monitor command does. Issues "io $aaaa" for the REQUIRED "address" argument (the bare "io" verb dumps every chip; this tool decodes the chip covering exactly one address), returning the chip's 64-byte register dump, its decoded VIC-II display state, and its sprite table. Every decoded-prose line this parser does not recognise is preserved verbatim and counted, never silently dropped or mapped onto a typed field. "io" carries no build-time guard, but degrades per-chip at runtime with its own two fixed strings when a chip has nothing to report -- reported as a named chip fact, never mistaken for a missing build capability. The decoded display state and sprite table are VIC-II only; an address covered by another chip (e.g. CIA1, CIA2, SID) is refused by name, with its register dump reported as having read cleanly.

address.description: REQUIRED. The C64 address whose covering chip is decoded: number, $hex string or symbol name.

tools.name: vice_program_load
tools.description: Loads a program file into RAM with VICE's own text-monitor command `load "<file>" 0 [<address>]`, without resetting or starting the machine. The MCP server reads the file at `path` and streams it to the broker, which stages it; the command names only the staged file, so the path itself never crosses the socket. Without `address`, VICE loads at the address in the file's two-byte header. Use vice_autostart instead to reset, load and run. Halts the machine for the duration of the command.

path.description: Path to the program file on the MCP server's side. Relative paths resolve against the MCP server's working directory.

address.description: OPTIONAL. Load address overriding the file's two-byte header, as VICE's `load` allows: number, $hex string or symbol name.
